Theme

the Mother of God noun

also Mother of God, Theotokos, the Virgin Mary, Our Lady, the Blessed Virgin

late Latin

Cod. Just. 1.1.6 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. Virgin Mary: Deipara Virgō (Tursellinus, 1652)

Deipara, Deiparae f.

noun, first declension

“She who bore God”, Latin for Greek Θεοτόκος, the title confirmed at Ephesus (431) and used in both churches.

Other words

  • Theotocos, Theotocī f. — Theotokos

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Cod. Just. 1.1.6: theotocos virgō Marīa (Lewis & Short)

    The Greek title itself, in Latin letters.

  • Deī Genetrīx, Deī Genetrīcis f. — Mother of God

    also used · medieval

    The usual name in the Latin liturgy; genetrīx, mother, is classical (Enn., Verg.; Lewis & Short). Its early attestation was not checked here.

Examples

  • Et unde hoc mihi, ut veniat māter Dominī meī ad mē?

    And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?Vulg. Lc. 1.43

See also the Annunciation, Christmas, God.
